reason: E1 shows that PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles prepared by a one-step colloid route exhibit isolated Pt/Pd sites, charge transfer to Pt/Pd, and enhanced nitrobenzene hydrogenation activity, directly supporting the link between isolation, electronic modification, and activity. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence that varying precursor mobility (low vs. high) controls the degree of isolation or agglomeration, leaving the central causal premise of the hypothesis unsupported.
premises: Inhibited precursor mobility during synthesis yields atomic-scale isolation of noble metal sites in HEA nanoparticles
Atomic-scale isolation of noble metals promotes charge transfer from neighboring transition metals
Charge transfer modifies the electronic structure of noble metal sites
Modified electronic structure enhances catalytic activity for nitrobenzene hydrogenation
Higher precursor mobility leads to noble metal agglomeration and inferior performance
